page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache resources consist of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and 8-bit integer operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-threaded compression and decompression capabilities, with gzip compression reaching 36.79 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 15.35 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 226.88 GB/sec. Passmark CPU testing yields a strong score of 53875.1, while database operations and Redis SET operations perform in the average tier, with Redis handling 60.05 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is strong at 61.65 GB/sec.

While prompt processing for language models is strong to average, text generation for larger models represents a performance tradeoff, dropping to a weak 2.77 tokens/sec on a 70B model due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, though it is Premium Storage capable. This resource profile is suited for general-purpose workloads, web serving, multi-threaded data processing, and moderate database operations.
